name: Neptune from Voyager 2, August 25, 1989, 20:33 UTC
blurb: The windiest planet in the solar system, about 49,500 kilometers across at the equator. Seen by Voyager 2's wide-angle camera through orange, green, blue and violet filters: visible light only, 0.40 to 0.62 µm.
story: The whole of Neptune, as a crescent, from about 1.1 million kilometers from Neptune's center, 17 hours after Voyager 2's closest approach to Neptune on August 25, 1989. Voyager 2 was the first spacecraft to fly by Neptune, in 1989, when a huge storm called the Great Dark Spot swirled in its southern hemisphere; that storm has since disappeared.
